questions.question:
**Direction: Choose the appropriate idiomatic expression for the given sentence:**

The man tried to dispose of his old car ______.

options.text: to lay his cards on the table

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. 'by hook or by crook'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"by hook or by crook"** means to accomplish something by any means necessary, whether fair or foul; using any possible method to achieve a goal. (किसी भी तरह से)

 
 
• **Example: **He was determined to win the race by hook or by crook.
 
 
 
• **"by hook or by crook"** refers to doing whatever it takes to get something done. (किसी भी तरह से)
 
 
• **Example: **The man tried to dispose of his old car by hook or by crook.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **by hook or by crook**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **in for a few pennies** (कुछ पैसों के लिए): This phrase generally is not idiomatic, and it doesn't fit the context of the sentence.

 
 
• **Example:** N/A, as this is not a common idiom.
 
 
 
• **to lay his cards on the table** (खुलकर सामने रखना): This idiom means to be open and honest about one's intentions or plans.
 
 
• **Example:** He laid his cards on the table and told them the truth about his plans.
 
 
 
• **by throwing cold water** (बदम बनाना): This idiom means to discourage or dampen someone's enthusiasm.
 
 
• **Example:** She threw cold water on his proposal by pointing out all its flaws.

questions.question:
**Pick out the most effective pair of words from the given options to make the sentence meaningfully complete.**

He was an ____________musician, has been awarded with the Bharat Ratna during World War I and ______ with the title of “Modern Tansen”.
questions.solution:
Correct answer: **Option: 2- accomplished, honoured**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Grammatically and contextually, **accomplished and honoured** fits in the blanks.
 
• The word **'accomplished'** is an **adjective** meaning ***'very good at a particular thing; having a lot of skills'***.
 
 
• **Example:** Ram is one of the school's most accomplished graduates.
 
 
 
• The word **'honoured'** is a **verb** meaning ***'to give public praise, an award or a title to somebody for something they have done'.***
 
 
• **Example: **Krish was honoured for his bravery.*** ***
 
 
 
• Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct sentence is- ***'He was an accomplished musician, has been awarded with the Bharat Ratna during World War I and honoured with the title of “Modern Tansen”.***'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The word **'o****bdurate'** is an **adjective** meaning ***'stubborn'.***
 
• The word **'proclaimed' **is a **verb **meaning ***'to publicly and officially tell people about something important'***.
 
• **Outstanding, accomplished and impressive** are synonymous.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with suitable tense.

If you ______ me, I would have given you the book.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"had asked"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct answer is "had asked." This is the correct past tense form of the verb "ask" to match the past conditional mood of the sentence, "If you had asked me."**
 
• **"has asked"** is in the present perfect tense, which is not appropriate in this sentence as it refers to a past hypothetical situation.
 
• **"had ask"** is a grammatically incorrect form of the verb "ask." The past participle form of "ask" is "asked."
 
• ​**"would ask"** is in the future tense, which is not appropriate in this sentence as it refers to a past hypothetical situation.

***Correct Sentence:***__ If you had asked me, I would have given you the book.

questions.question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate word. Choose the correct alternative.

There is always an ______ to a stated theory.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is “**exception**”.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Exception**: This is the correct answer. 
 
• An **exception** refers to something that deviates from the norm or contradicts a rule or theory. 
 
 
• **For example, **"*The theory that all swans are white was proven false when a black swan was discovered, which was an **exception** to the theory."*
 
 

**Hence, the correct answer is** “*exception*”

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Let's see the other given options:**

 
• **Placid**: This word means calm, peaceful, and undisturbed. It is not an appropriate choice to fill in the blank in the given sentence. 

 
 
• **An example of using placid in a sentence is** *"The lake was **placid**, reflecting the colors of the sunset."*
 
 
 
• **Enmity**: This word means hostility, animosity, or hatred. It is not an appropriate choice to fill in the blank in the given sentence. 
 
 
• **An example of using enmity in a sentence is** *"The **enmity** between the two nations led to a long-standing conflict."*
 
 
 
• **Eulogy**: This word refers to a speech or writing in praise of someone who has died. It is not an appropriate choice to fill in the blank in the given sentence. 
 
 
• **An example of using eulogy in a sentence is ***"The minister gave a moving **eulogy** at the funeral, celebrating the life of the deceased."*

questions.question:
Direction: Choose the appropriate phrase preposition to fill in the blank.

A single judge of the High court held that the land was given to the appellant by her husband ___________________________ maintenance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**in lieu of".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Meanings of the phrase given in the options:

 
 
• **In lieu of **means "instead of or in place of someone (**किसी के स्थान पर या किसी की जगह में**)**".**

 
 
• **Example:** *The company is allowing workers to receive cash **in lieu of** vacation time.*
 
 
 
• Here, the appropriate phrasal verb is 'in lieu of', as the above sentence means** a single judge of the court said that the claimant ****was given the land by her husband in place of maintenance.**
 
 
 
• All the other options are eliminated because they are not a phrase.

Therefore, option 2 is the correct answer. 

Complete Sentence__:* **A Single Judge of the High Court held that the land was given to the appellant by her husband __in lieu of__ maintenance.*

questions.question:
**Fill in the gap correctly:**

The shirt cost me _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Five Thousand rupees**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Five thousand**" is a **number** and "**rupee**" is a **unit of currency**.
 
• So it should be written as "**five thousand rupees**" or "**5,000 rupees**"
 
• The word "**rupee**" should be in its **plural** form since it is **more than one**, and "**five thousand**" should be **singular**.

Thus, ***option 3*** is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence**__: *The shirt cost me **five thousand rupees**.*

questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with a suitable article from the given alternatives.

We are trying to give _______ incredible performance at the farewell day function.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "an"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The indefinite article** "an"** is used before a noun that begins with a vowel sound,
 
• In the above sentence "incredible" begins with the vowel sound "ih."
 
• So, the most suitable article is "an"

***Correct Sentence:***__ We are trying to give **an** incredible performance at the farewell day function.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **"The" is the definite article.** It is used to refer to a specific or particular noun, and implies that the reader or listener already knows what is being referred to.* For example: "The car that hit my fence was red."*
 
• **"A" and "An" are indefinite articles**. They are used to refer to any one member of a group of things, but not necessarily a specific member. The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the sound of the noun that follows, with "a" being used before nouns that start with a consonant sound, and "an" being used before nouns that start with a vowel sound. **For example:** "A dog is barking outside" and "An apple a day keeps the doctor away."
 
• No article, or the zero article, is used to refer to nouns in a general sense, rather than a specific member of the group. **For example: **"Dogs are loyal pets."

questions.question:
Direction: Choose the correct word to fill up the blanks from the alternatives.

Asvat ______ TV when her husband came.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: '**was watching'.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence has two events occurring:
 
 
• *Asvat was watching TV.*
 
• *Her husband came home.*
 
 
 
• In the sentences where two events occur simultaneously and one occurs before and continues while the other has happened, we use the past continuous tense.
 
• From the given options, it is clear that we need to use the past continuous tense of the verb** 'watch'****.**
 
• So, was watching is the correct tense form for the given blank.
 
• Hence, option 2 is the correct answer. 

Complete sentence__ - *Asvat __**was watching**__** **TV when her husband came.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• The tense form of the other given options are as follows - 
 
 
• watch - simple present tense
 
• is watching - present continuous tense
 
• watched - past tense

questions.solution: The correct answer is "**among**" [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The correct **preposition** to use in this sentence is "**among**". • "**Among**" is used when referring to **distribution or distribution of something among a group of people or things**. • **Example**: The teacher distributed the candy **among** the students. • In this sentence, the sweets are being distributed among four children, so the correct **preposition** is "**among**." Thus, ***option 3*** is the correct answer. **Correct sentence**__: *Distribute the sweets equally **among** four children.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** __ • "**Between**" is used when referring to a specific relationship or comparison between two things. • **Example**: The book is **between** the two chairs. • "**In**" is used when referring to a specific location or container. • **Example**: The book is **in** the bag. • "**Through**" is used when referring to movement or an action done in a specific direction. • **Example**: We walked **through** the park. questions.question:
**Direction: Fill in the blanks with the appropriate article in the given sentence:**

There is ______ institution for ______ blind in this town and it teaches how to read ______ Braille.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'an, the, no article****.' **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The only articles in English are ‘the’ and ‘a/an’.
 
• We use the article "a or an" to indicate any non-specified member of a group or category.
 
• If a word begins with a vowel sound, then the correct article is 'an'; otherwise, if it begins with a consonantal sound, the correct article is 'a'.
 
• The word **"institute"** starts with a vowel sound **"i" **and the sentence is referring to any unspecific institute, so must use **"an"** in the first blank.
 
• We are talking about an institution which is particularly for **"blind people"** so we must use "the" in the second blank.
 
• We do not use articles with the names of languages, thus, there will be no article before **'Braille'.**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is Option 2.

 ​

​Correct sentence__: *There is __**an**__ institution for __**the**__ blind in this town and it teaches how to read Braille.*
